chapter: Les Hite, Sebastian's and Duke Ellington
title: Tunes from the film and versions of Rockin' in Rhythm
summary: Royal recalls Check and Double Check and Rockin' in Rhythm and how the latter grew in versions.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So, do you remember what all you played in "Check and Double Check"? What tunes? (inaudible)?
The tune "Check and Double Check" was one of them. I can't remember the rest. That's a long time --
Was "Rockin' in and Rhythm" (inaudible)? in that movie?
"Rockin' in and Rhythm." That was it.
"Check and Double Check" was one and "Rockin' and Rhythm" was another one. That was two of them.
So it was on violin (inaudible)? Because that you originally played it. I was mentioning to you what Bill Berry (PHONETIC) said --
Oh, I played it on saxophone, too, at various times because I worked in a band -- a whole lot of times after that and that was always part of his book.
Bill Berry was so impressed (inaudible). that you knew it from 1930.

There was two or three different versions of "Rockin' in Rhythm" that was added onto it and added onto it until it is actually what it is now, to where you heard it the first time you heard it. That was two and three revised parts that had been added onto it and made it --
